    Positive definite quadratic maps #

    Multiplication by a positive scalar preserves and reflects positive-definiteness when the scalar action preserves and reflects strict inequalities on values. In particular, symmetrizing a bilinear form preserves positive-definiteness of its quadratic map, since the diagonal values are doubled. A diagonal form is positive definite exactly when its weights are positive.

    A positive definite quadratic form on a finitely generated free ℤ-module takes each of its values only finitely often: the sets {x | q x ≤ n} and {x | q x = n} are finite. This is the finiteness that makes "the vectors of norm n" of a positive definite lattice a finite list, and the one that turns an orbit lying in a level set into a periodic orbit.

    Main results #

    • QuadraticMap.posDef_smul_iff_of_pos: a quadratic map is positive definite if and only if its multiple by a positive scalar is positive definite.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.posDef_toQuadraticMap_add_flip_iff: symmetrizing a bilinear form preserves and reflects positive-definiteness of its quadratic map.
    • QuadraticMap.posDef_weightedSumSquares_iff: a diagonal form over a linearly ordered ring is positive definite exactly when all of its weights are positive.
    • QuadraticMap.PosDef.finite_setOf_apply_le: a positive definite quadratic form on a finitely generated free ℤ-module has only finitely many vectors of value at most n.
    • QuadraticMap.PosDef.finite_setOf_apply_eq: consequently only finitely many vectors of value exactly n.

    The finiteness results live in the root QuadraticMap.PosDef namespace so that they are available by dot notation on a QuadraticForm.PosDef hypothesis.

    Implementation notes #

    The finiteness argument stays inside ℤ; no rational or real coefficients, no compactness, and no diagonalization enter. Write B for the polar form, which is symmetric with B x x = 2 * q x, hence nonnegative, and let b be a basis. The coordinates of x in the dual-like map T x = fun i ↦ B x (b i) are bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz for a positive semidefinite symmetric form (LinearMap.BilinForm.apply_sq_le_of_symm), since (B x (b i)) ^ 2 ≤ B x x * B (b i) (b i) and the right-hand side is bounded once q x is. The map T is injective: a vector it kills is orthogonal to a basis, hence to itself, hence isotropic, hence zero. So the set in question is the preimage under an injective map of a box of integer vectors.

    Note that T is not claimed to be surjective, and need not be: the polar form of a positive definite integral quadratic form is generally not unimodular. Injectivity is all the argument uses.

    theorem QuadraticMap.posDef_smul_iff_of_pos {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} [CommSemiring R] [Preorder R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [PartialOrder N] [Module R N] [PosSMulStrictMono R N] [PosSMulReflectLT R N] (Q : QuadraticMap R M N) {a : R} (ha : 0 < a) :
    (a • Q).PosDef ↔ Q.PosDef

    Multiplication by a positive scalar preserves and reflects positive-definiteness when the scalar action preserves and reflects strict inequalities on values.

    theorem QuadraticMap.posDef_weightedSumSquares_iff {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] {R : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] (w : ι → R) :
    (weightedSumSquares R w).PosDef ↔ ∀ (i : ι), 0 < w i

    A diagonal form ⟨w₁, …, wₙ⟩ over a linearly ordered ring is positive definite exactly when all of its weights are positive.

    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.posDef_toQuadraticMap_add_flip_iff {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M) :
    (BilinMap.toQuadraticMap (B + B.flip)).PosDef ↔ (BilinMap.toQuadraticMap B).PosDef

    Symmetrization preserves and reflects positive-definiteness of a bilinear form's quadratic map.

    theorem QuadraticMap.PosDef.finite_setOf_apply_le {M : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup M] [Module.Free ℤ M] [Module.Finite ℤ M] {q : QuadraticForm ℤ M} (hq : PosDef q) (n : ℤ) :
    {x : M | q x ≤ n}.Finite

    A positive definite integral quadratic form has finitely many vectors of bounded value. For a positive definite quadratic form q on a finitely generated free ℤ-module and any integer n, only finitely many vectors satisfy q x ≤ n.

    source
    theorem QuadraticMap.PosDef.finite_setOf_apply_eq {M : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup M] [Module.Free ℤ M] [Module.Finite ℤ M] {q : QuadraticForm ℤ M} (hq : PosDef q) (n : ℤ) :
    {x : M | q x = n}.Finite

    A positive definite integral quadratic form takes each value finitely often. For a positive definite quadratic form q on a finitely generated free ℤ-module, only finitely many vectors satisfy q x = n; for a positive definite lattice this is the finiteness of the set of vectors of a given norm.
